rows.label: Concept
rows.text: A **capacitor** is two conductors separated by an insulator; charging places ±Q on its plates with potential difference V. **Capacitance** $C = Q/V$ (farad) measures charge stored per volt — fixed by geometry and dielectric, not by charge or voltage. Practical values run in μF and pF. Capacitors smooth power supplies, tune radios, store flash/defibrillator energy, and block DC while passing AC (NEB 2024, 2m).…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - C = Q/V; unit farad; 1 μF = 10⁻⁶ F; 1 pF = 10⁻¹² F - Q = CV; V = Q/C

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **C is a geometry constant:** doubling Q doubles V, leaving C = Q/V unchanged.  ·  **Farad is huge:** practical capacitors are μF or pF.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Standard dielectric breakdown of dry air occurs at an electric field of E_max ≈ 3 × 10^6 V/m; beyond this, air ionizes and spark discharge neutralizes the plates.  ·  In electrostatic equilibrium, the surface of any conducting capacitor plate is an equipotential surface.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Defibrillator*** — a capacitor dumps stored energy through the chest in milliseconds.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Verified PYQ: four uses of capacitors (2024, 2m). The 2023/2024 5m capacitance-derivation questions are cited under Topic 94.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Derive C = 4πε₀R for an isolated sphere.  ·  State the units, dimensions, and physical factors determining capacitance.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "Q = CV is the capacitor's Ohm's-law analogue."

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Numerical (2m): A 4 μF capacitor at 250 V. Find the charge.** — Q = CV = 4×10⁻⁶ × 250 = 10⁻³ C = 1 mC.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Charge Bucket A capacitor stores charge and energy in the electric field between two conductors. Its capacitance — charge per volt — is the "bucket size" of electrostatics, measured in farads, and it powers everything from camera flashes to computer memory.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts (NEB 2023, 2024) ### 2.1 Capacitor and capacitance A **capacitor** is a pair of conductors separated by an insulator (air or dielectric). Charging it places +Q on one plate and −Q on the other, creating a potential difference V. **Capacitance:** $$C = \frac{Q}{V} \qquad \text{SI unit: farad (F)}$$ — the charge stored per unit potential difference.…  ·  ## 3. Conceptual Relationships - **To Topic 94:** the parallel-plate geometry gives C = ε₀A/d explicitly. - **To Topic 95:** capacitors combine in series and parallel (opposite to resistors). - **To Topic 96:** U = ½CV² — the stored energy viewpoint.
